chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no Hadd (fixed penalty) for the one upon whom there is no Hadd, meaning, if an insane person were to slander a man, I do not see any penalty upon him, and if a man were to slander him, so he says to him, "O adulterer", there would be no Hadd upon him.'

key_terms.حَدّ: Fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.قَذَفَ: To slander or accuse of adultery

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the fixed penalty (Hadd) for slander when applied to or against an insane person?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'absence of penalty where there is no liability' (la hadda li-man la hadda 'alayh), highlighting the reciprocal nature of legal accountability in Shia jurisprudence. It clarifies that the Hadd for slander (Qadhf) is contingent upon the sanity and legal capacity of both the accuser and the accused, ensuring that the insane are neither punished for slandering nor protected from being slandered in a way that incurs liability on the slanderer. This ruling underscores the logical consistency of Islamic penal law, where the exemption from punishment for the insane extends to their interactions with sane individuals regarding specific fixed penalties.
